references.text: The Mosaic law on inheritance and the right of the firstborn: The firstborn shall receive a double portion of the inheritance. The man's request in Luke 12:13 concerns exactly the division of an estate between brothers, which was regulated in Deuteronomy 21:17.

The rules on inheritance division in Israel, where Moses establishes inheritance laws following the complaint of Zelophehad's daughters. The man in Luke 12:13 asks Jesus to settle an inheritance dispute, just as Moses was asked to resolve inheritance questions in Numbers 27:1-11.

When Moses intervened in a conflict between two Hebrews, one of them asked, 'Who made you ruler and judge over us?' This scene has a parallel to Luke 12:13, where a man in the crowd asks Jesus to act as judge in an inheritance case. Jesus rejects this role in a similar way (cf. Exodus 2:14).
Jesus' answer to the request: 'Who made me your judge or arbitrator?' Jesus refuses to serve as an inheritance judge, which is the direct response to the request in Luke 12:13. See Luke 12:14.
Jesus uses the occasion from Luke 12:13 to warn against greed: 'Watch out! Be on your guard against all kinds of greed; life does not consist in an abundance of possessions.' See Luke 12:15.

Paul warns against love of money and points out that 'godliness with contentment is great gain'. The man's demand for inheritance division in Luke 12:13 illustrates the attitude Paul warns against in 1 Timothy 6:6-10.
Jesus' call to sell possessions and give to the poor, and to store up treasures in heaven. This contrasts with the earthly concern over inheritance in Luke 12:13. See Luke 12:33-34.
'Do not let love of money rule your life, but be content with what you have.' The man's focus on his inheritance in Luke 12:13 shows an attitude that Hebrews 13:5 warns against.
The crowd sought Jesus for material gain (bread), and Jesus corrected them to seek spiritual food. Similarly, in Luke 12:13 the man approaches Jesus with a purely material concern. See John 6:26-27.

Jesus says, 'My kingdom is not of this world.' The man's request in Luke 12:13 to settle an earthly inheritance dispute shows a misunderstanding of Jesus' role and mission, which Jesus clarifies in John 18:36.
